scope: Artifact 03-test-spec, 04-validate-existing, 06-implement and 00-intro (node-fix-bug, claude-sonnet-5-5, ShipLoop 1.3.0 build 28b27f7ca5fb), checked against main da9e2e75 (1.5.0) by symbol and by offline renders at 66/~165/190-char run dirs (SP/eff2/render-specimpl-real). Answers: (1) the focused-ID gate did not refuse; check-only refused twice, for a missing `requirement` key (copied example R-3) and for R-3 absent from spec.md (model wrote it): SPEC-3, SPEC-6. (2) The oracle was independent (value from the request, no source opened); guidance adequate for stated values, script proof comes at test: SPEC-10. (3) Implement commands came from memory of the step plan; no read; lint never run; npm test piped: SPEC-1, SPEC-2, SPEC-5. (4) Model-judged duty inventory: SPEC-9. (5) Cold gaps: step paths/skills/check and lint commands (SPEC-2), R-ids and loop start (SPEC-3, SPEC-4). (6) A 20,000 cut removes nothing printed; the file loses RULES, Pause, Halt and the lint command: SPEC-8. (7) Wording and symbols are in each proposal.

findings.where: skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_loops.py (_build, check_loop_packet), shiploop_loop_contract.py (contract), shiploop_stage_spec.py (COMPLETE_RUNS, implement.complete_runs), shiploop_test_loop.py (verify, stage_commands), shiploop_navigator.py (_CHECK_TEXT)
findings.observation: Both loops in 03/06 were receipts, not controls. Receipts show exit_checks [] and action_number 1 (trivial_streak 1, required_trivial_reviews 0). The work (result file, edit, npm test) ran before `until_loop_ephemeral.py start`; one `done` then reported exit satisfied, and check_loop_packet accepts on exit_assessment == satisfied. So every exit condition is the model's word. In implement, exit 2 rests on `npm test 2>&1 | grep -E ...` plus a notes line 'npm test exit 0 (7 pass)' (the pipe hides the exit code); the recorded check row `node --check src/paginate.js` ran later in a subshell and is not in the notes; `shiploop lint` was never run, yet the done report says 'no lint-relevant findings'. implement.complete_runs is ('loop-terminal','lint-gate'): nothing script-reruns the check commands until the test stage. The vendored runtime (0.8.3 per PROVENANCE.json) already supports exit_checks plus a verify_script the model runs in its own shell, so hooks see each command, and it refuses 'satisfied' without a recorded run after the last workspace change.
findings.proposal: 1) Add COMPLETE_RUNS entry 'check-rerun'; implement.complete_runs becomes ('loop-terminal','check-rerun','lint-gate'); _CHECK_TEXT['check-rerun'] = 'reruns the step plan's check commands and refuses done unless each exits 0'; the complete path calls test_loop.verify(root, state, item, action_id, 'implement', commands=[r for r in test_loop.stage_commands(state, 'implement', item)[0] if r['suite'] == 'check'], count=not check_only). 2) Define the term in implement duty 3: 'run every check command (the step plan's suite check rows, printed on the Step block)'. 3) After D-5, pass the same rows as exit_checks [{id:'K1', clause:'every recorded check command exits 0', command:<row command>}] through a new exit_checks keyword of loop_contract.contract (commands come only from the accepted step plan, so the contract still rebuilds from state and names no install path), compare packet['exit_checks'] in check_loop_packet, and keep verify_script and last_check_results in step 6.5's lean done print.
findings.generic_ok: Yes. Uses the plan's own suite=check rows (lint, type or build commands); no domain words.
findings.risk: A slow or flaky check row now refuses done: restrict to suite check rows (focused and regression cannot pass before the test stage), run with count=not check_only so only real refusals count toward MAX_REFUSED_RUNS. Stage 3 changes the vendored-runtime contract surface (D-5) and the lean print (6.5).
findings.plan_ref: none (principle 11 'Exits are script-run' covers plan steps only); touches 6.5, D-5; suggest a W7.3 step
findings.est_effect: Fidelity, not minutes: a failing check is refused at implement complete, not at test one Improve review later; also forces work -> verify -> done order for observable exits. Cost: one script run of the check rows per step. Time not measured.

findings.observation: Implement cannot be done from the printed packet alone (S-6). _step_lines is called only by the full render, never by packet_head, and the head's hand-off fallback drops criteria and test_cases whenever the head would pass 16,000. Rendered on main da9e2e75 at run dirs of 66, about 165 and 190 chars: implement head 15,912 / 17,284 / 17,648 chars, with no 'Step S1' line, no step paths, no step skills, no check commands and no lint command. The full packet's Step line carries only the task. The literal lint command ('Lint each implementation step (report-only): ...') is the last line of the file (offset 22,100 of 22,388 at about 165 chars; _lint_lines is not called by packet_head). Duty 3 says run `shiploop lint --action` with no command; exit 1 says 'only the step's paths changed' and exit 4 'whether each of the step's skills was used', but neither list is printed anywhere: with a plan whose step lists a skill, no implement packet (head or file) prints it. In the artifact the model acted from memory of its own step-plan: 3 tool calls, 0 reads of the packet file, no lint.
findings.proposal: In packet_head add *_step_lines(...) and make _step_lines print the whole Step block (about 300 to 500 chars) with the lint command beside it: 'Step S1 (1 of 1), the only work for this packet: <task>' / 'Step paths (change only these): src/paginate.js' / 'Step skills (use each; the summary says whether you did): none' / 'Check commands (run each after every edit; exit codes to RUN/notes/<action>.md): node --check src/paginate.js' / 'Lint this step (report-only): <the existing literal lint command>'. Duty 3 then reads: 'After each edit run the Check commands and the Lint command on the Step block; write each exit code in RUN/notes/<action>.md.' Rows come from loops.current_step and test_loop.stage_commands (suite check); lint line from lint.render_lines.
findings.generic_ok: Yes: ids, paths, skill names and commands all come from the accepted step plan.
findings.risk: Head is already over PRINT_LIMIT at about 165 chars, so the +300 to 500 chars needs the named offset the plan requires (1.2). Several suites pin the Step line text; the lint line prints only when the run option is fix or report.
findings.plan_ref: 1.2 P1 (implement Step line), 7.1(c) (each step's commands), per-packet table row 11
findings.est_effect: +300 to 500 chars on the implement head; a cold implement no longer has to open the step-plan result (about 5 KB) to learn paths, skills and commands; the lint command survives any file cut. No change on a warm context.

findings.observation: The focused-ID gate did not refuse (TC-1 matched). Two other check-only refusals did. (1) The model dropped `requirement` from its row although the template and duty 2 list it. The refusal prints a literal example row with requirement 'R-3' (the template prints 'R-1'), and the model said 'Requirement is expected as R-3; I'll use it'. (2) R-3 had no entry in HOME/spec.md (the seed never wrote one; the refusal names the file, not what it holds), so the model wrote a new spec.md with R-3, which ShipLoop commits with HOME. The literal example values in HANDOFF_SHAPES['test_cases'] (id TC-1, criterion C1, requirement R-1) pass the gate wherever such ids exist, so a copied example is accepted silently and can map a case to the wrong requirement. The Checked-by line already says 'a requirement with no entry in HOME/spec.md', but the spec's R-ids are printed only inside the quoted spec, which drops out of the head whenever the head passes 16,000 (test-spec stayed under it at the run dirs measured, so only a large spec triggers this).
findings.proposal: (a) _TEST_CASE_SHAPE: replace the literal row with placeholders: 'test_cases are [{"id": "<a focused command ID>", "criterion": "<a step-plan criterion id>", "requirement": "<R-n listed in HOME/spec.md>", "oracle": ..., "red": ..., "green": ...}]'. (b) HANDOFF_SHAPES['test_cases'] and _result_template for test-spec: one row per focused ID with the id filled from the step plan, criterion and requirement as placeholders added to HANDOFF_PLACEHOLDERS. (c) The unknown-requirement refusal in check_test_cases appends 'HOME/spec.md lists R-1, R-2, ...' (knowledge._ids over entries) or 'HOME/spec.md lists no R-n entry' when empty. (d) Print the same R-id list (id plus first 60 chars) in the test-spec head, derived from knowledge.entries.
findings.generic_ok: Yes; ids come from the step plan and HOME/spec.md.
findings.risk: Tests use R-3/TC-1 as data (fine) and pin HANDOFF_PLACEHOLDERS; an empty spec still needs a rule for the model (record an assumption or report revise) which the artifact's seed-only case does not settle.
findings.plan_ref: 7.1(a) gate vocabulary printed from the validators' own tables; 8.1
findings.est_effect: Saves two check-only round trips (about 10 to 15 s) on a cold test-spec and removes a silent requirement mis-mapping and a model-written spec entry; bytes about zero.

findings.where: skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_loops.py (invoke_lines; on branch -loop- HOST_LINE, INVOKE_LINE, start_command)
findings.observation: The step-plan stage (01) called the Skill tool with skill until-loop and got '<tool_use_error>Unknown skill: until-loop</tool_use_error>', then grepped ADAPTER.md (2,550 chars) for the start command; test-spec and implement then started the runtime script directly from memory. Main still prints 'on Claude Code, the Skill tool with skill until-loop ...', and branch -loop- 0d462ca4 keeps 'Claude Code: the Skill tool, skill until-loop, with that argument' and only the other hosts get the literal command. A cleared Claude model repeats the failed call and the ADAPTER read at every cold start.
findings.proposal: HOST_LINE: 'Claude Code: the Skill tool, skill "until-loop", with that argument; if it reports an unknown skill, or on any other host, run this in the foreground, then follow each packet it prints (run its done_argv as printed) until the receipt says complete or stopped:' followed by start_command(...).
findings.risk: None for hosts with the skill. Whether the unknown-skill case is specific to the harness's --plugin-dir install is not measured.
findings.est_effect: Removes one failed tool call and one ADAPTER grep (about 2.5 KB) per cold loop start on installs without the until-loop skill.

findings.observation: In 03 and 06 every ShipLoop and runtime command used shell variables for the executable and paths (`R=...; A=...; SC=...; python3 $SC complete ...`, `python3 $P start ...`): 11 of 11 (7 complete, 4 runtime). All 7 complete calls were piped to `head` and the 4 runtime calls to `python3 -c`, although RULES says 'Run ShipLoop commands in the foreground, unpiped'. _verb returns None for any command with a pipe/chain token or without a token whose basename is `shiploop` under scripts/, so the status hook recognised none of them (keepalive patterns likewise: inferred from plan 5.6). The runtime `done` return was cut to its `status` field, so its `instruction` was never read (terminal here; a non-terminal return would be lost).
findings.proposal: Keep 3.2(d) and give it its reason so it is followed: 'Run ShipLoop and loop commands exactly as printed: no pipe, redirect, ; chain, shell variable or wrapper (a pipe hides the exit code, and the status hook only recognises the printed form).' The printed complete command is 330+ chars at a 190-char run dir, which is why the model abbreviates; after 3.2(a)/(b) shrink it, recount variable use in the 1.3 buckets and reopen D-11 (shorter run root and ids) if more than half of commands still use variables.
findings.risk: A bullet alone may not hold (the existing 'unpiped' bullet was ignored 7 of 7); a rule that makes a model refuse is barred (rule 13), so keep it a statement of the printed form, not a prohibition with a penalty.
findings.est_effect: Status hook and keepalive see the commands again; no byte change. Compliance effect not measured.

findings.observation: check_test_cases checks ids both ways, criterion membership and requirement existence, not the first exit condition ('every completion criterion has at least one test case, or a justified not-applicable'). C2 (suite stays green) had no case, check-only accepted, and the justification is one clause of the free-text summary. The step plan already records what confirms C2: test_commands row {command: npm test, criteria: [C2], suite: regression}.
findings.proposal: After the criterion check: covered = {case criterion} | {c for row in plan test_commands if row suite != 'focused' for c in row criteria}. For each criterion not in covered print a counted notice, not a refusal first: 'Criterion C3 has no test case and no recorded non-focused command lists it in criteria: add a case, add the command to the step plan, or record an assumptions open item naming the inspection that confirms it.' Duty 6 gains: 'A criterion confirmed only by a recorded command needs no case; that command's criteria field is the proof.'
findings.risk: False notices for inspection-only criteria; keep it a notice until the journal shows none.
findings.plan_ref: 7.1(c) coverage-by-mention gates as counted notices first
findings.est_effect: Makes exit 1 script-run for the common case; no bytes.

findings.observation: Two sentences the artifact shows to be wrong. (1) Every Checked-by line ends '`complete --check-only` prints every refusal first'; test-spec needed two sequential check-only rounds (shape, then requirement), each showing one fault. (2) WORK['test-spec'] says 'Do duty items 1-6' of a 7-item duty list (item 7, the summary/evidence_refs duty, is outside the loop) and WORK['implement'] 'duty items 1-4' of 7 (Services, Unachievable, Inline are outside).
findings.proposal: _checked_line tail: 'A refusal does not advance the run: fix the cause and run the same command again; `complete --check-only` runs the same gates without accepting and prints the first refusal, so repeat it until it accepts.' For WORK, fill the range from the parsed duty count with a per-stage override table (implement: 1-4 plus 5 when the step touches a service) and a test that pins the table to the duty count, so a renumbering fails a test, not a model.
findings.risk: loops.WORK is coupled to duty numbering (plan section 10); keep the pin test.
findings.plan_ref: 8.1 (false _checked_line; Work lines citing only part of the duty items)
findings.est_effect: Removes a false promise (one wasted round trip in this run); about -40 chars.

findings.observation: Rendered offsets on main (node-fix-bug, inline). test-spec whole file 15,788 chars at a run dir of about 165 chars, 212 under the 16,000 switch; at 190 chars it is 16,334 and prints as a 12,778-char head, so the flip is at about a 175-char run dir. In the whole file the duties start at 12,840 and RULES at 14,639, after hand-offs and the request. implement file 22,388: duties at 14,342, Code craft 17,261, RULES 20,951, Pause 21,490, Halt 21,821, lint command 22,100. A 20,000 cut of the file removes RULES, Pause, Halt and the only literal lint command (2,388 chars); a 20,000 cut of what is printed removes nothing (test-spec 15,788 whole, implement head 17,284, validate-existing prints no packet on the happy path). The binding limits are the 16,000 whole/head switch and the head's hand-off fallback, not the host cut. No line of 50+ chars repeats inside the test-spec, validate-existing or implement renders (checked by script).
findings.proposal: Give the file the head's order: header, goal, loop block, duties, Code craft, RULES, Step block with lint command, Pause/Halt, then hand-offs, request, last-accepted, so a cut file loses only quoted material (principle 10). Journal the 16,000 cliff per stage in the 1.2 table.
findings.risk: Layout pins in packet-recut and completeness suites; do not reorder anything the status hook reads in the first 16,000 bytes.
findings.est_effect: No bytes; protects the lint command, RULES and Pause/Halt from any cut at 20,000 on a file read through a cutting host tool.

findings.observation: Duties checked by no script (the owner wants exits script-run). test-spec: exit 1 criterion coverage (SPEC-6); exit 2 oracle independence is checked for non-blank only (the script proof comes later at test: base run and mutants); duty 4 failure/boundary/rejection cases and the summary's 'rejection cases already exist' (written without opening any test file in that stage); duty 6 later-phase assumptions; duty 7 harness decisions. implement: exit 1 paths (Checked-by lists a path gate only for items with no test command and only non-code paths, so a normal code item has none); exit 2 (SPEC-1); exit 4 skills and not_covered (the template calls not_covered 'Optional', the exit says 'the result lists'; the model answered in summary prose); the notes file of exit codes has no reader; the 'same check still fails after 7 genuine fix attempts' stop (stage_spec comment: 'No script counts the attempts; the model applies it'). validate-existing happy path: fully script-run (works well); on a mismatch the route (check wrong vs fact wrong) is model-judged and only the rerun at complete is script-run.
findings.proposal: Script-run: SPEC-1 (check commands), SPEC-6 (criteria). Counted notices first: summary must name each skill the step plan lists (needs SPEC-2 so the model sees the list), not_covered present or explicitly none. Needs a design call: a per-step base tree recorded at implement entry (entry_runs) so exit 1 can compare changed paths with the step's paths. The 7-attempt stop: once exit_checks exist (SPEC-1 stage 3) the receipt's last_check_results and action_number let ShipLoop verify a revise that cites 7 failures; until then leave it as the owner's S-10 carve-out and say in the journal that it is model-applied. Cut the 'write each exit code in notes' duty when exit_checks records them.
findings.risk: Per-step base needs a state field and a migration rule for runs in flight (refuse old, per rule 3); notices for skills are text matching, so keep them non-refusing.
findings.est_effect: Inventory for the owner; effect depends on the items adopted.

findings.observation: Duty 3 ('Oracle from the requirement's text, never the code') is clear and the model's oracle was independent: it took the expected object from the request and never opened src/paginate.js in that stage. But the placeholder '<what observes the behaviour, and where>' asks for the mechanism, not the source of the expected value; the model added 'expected values taken from the request text' unprompted. Independence is proven by script only later (test base run: no new test may pass on the unfixed code; mutation gate), and not for new code or red_na cases. The case had a stated value; a computed value is untested here.
findings.proposal: _ORACLE_PLACEHOLDER = '<what observes the behaviour, where, and where its expected value comes from: request text, a spec R-n, or a tool's printed output>'. Keep duty 3. This is the oracle half of 7.2's copied/run/derived rule, usable without the optional derivations field.
findings.risk: Placeholder is gate-pinned (HANDOFF_PLACEHOLDERS) and about 230 text pins exist; the effect needs a second app with computed values (7.2 exit 2).
findings.est_effect: About +60 chars on test-spec; effect on oracle copying not measured.

findings.where: SP/artrev/00-intro.md (and the page builder behind it)
findings.observation: Five statements on the page do not match the recorded run. (1) 'each run as one Until Loop that ShipLoop's packet invokes by name': the Skill call failed (SPEC-4) and test-spec and implement ran start plus one done after the work, exit_checks [], so the loop did not iterate or verify. (2) 'Packets written: 13 (209,452 characters on disk)' but the comparison table's 'now' column sums to 148,458 (test-spec 12,833 there, 17,134 written in its section; implement 20,009 vs 24,870): an unlabelled second unit, probably an offline short-path render. (3) The 'What reached the model' lines (test-spec 7,361, implement 4,547 chars) describe the 1.3.0 head; main 1.5.0 prints 12,778 to 17,648 chars with duties, Code craft, RULES and the loop block, so those lines no longer describe main. (4) The run is inline and warm: the model wrote the step plan itself, so implement's 3 tool calls and 0 packet reads say nothing about a cleared context (S-6). (5) The diagram shows 'M->>U: loop: change the step's paths, run checks and lint' but no lint ran.
findings.proposal: Edit the intro: say 'the packet names the Skill tool; here it failed and the model started the runtime script from ADAPTER.md'; label the table 'offline render, short path, characters' and add a column of live written sizes; add 'build 28b27f7ca5fb predates the head change on main' beside the 'What reached the model' lines; add a 'warm context' badge to the inline run; change the diagram note to 'loop: start, one done, receipt checked' until exit_checks exist.
findings.est_effect: Prevents decisions on mixed units and on a loop that did not run as drawn.

findings.observation: The script-recorded validate-existing summary is 'ShipLoop ran every expectation check on the unchanged checkout and each matched its state; validate-existing was recorded without running it. Records: <path>'. The status Done line cuts it mid-word ('...recorded without running i...'), 'without running it' reads as if the checks were skipped, and in implement's packet the record path appears three times (Results this stage builds on, Last accepted summary, Evidence references).
findings.proposal: Summary = 'All expectation checks matched on the unchanged checkout (script-run, no model turn).' with the record only in evidence_refs; the Results list already names it as 'check record'. Under 100 chars, so status and narrative do not cut it.
findings.risk: Tests pin the summary text; low.
findings.plan_ref: 2.2 (shorten Last accepted transition; evidence as symbols)
findings.est_effect: About -100 chars in the next packet and a clean status line.

works_well: validate-existing happy path (04): zero model turns, record written by `_validate_existing_entry` with per-check exit, summary and output path; E1 confirmed the bug reproduced before any edit. Keep and extend this pattern: it is the model for script-run exits.

`complete --check-only` caught both test-spec faults before the real complete, and the real complete was accepted first time in test-spec and implement (no refused real submission in either stage); keep the command in the loop's Work line.
Focused-ID gate (`check_test_cases`): both directions, with the missing or extra ids named; TC-1 matched at once.
The implement Step line (in the full packet) names the single task and the file; with a one-token fix the stage cost 3 tool calls and 17 s.

Independence of an oracle is proven by script after test-spec: the test stage's base run (no new ID may pass before the change) and mutation gate. Keep duty 3's wording 'from the requirement's text, never the code'.

Main 1.5.0 head already leads with duties, Code craft, RULES and the loop block (measured by render at 66, about 165 and 190 chars); the 1.3.0 head forced a grep of the file. 'Done when: every exit condition in the /until-loop argument below' now points at text that is in the head.
No 50-char line repeats inside test-spec, validate-existing or implement packets on main (script check), so within-packet dedupe has nothing left in these three.
not_measured: Cleared-context behaviour of these stages: the run is inline and warm (the model authored the step plan), so what a cleared model would read, skip or get wrong is inferred from renders, not observed (plan 3.7 battery measures it).

Script time of validate-existing's expectation checks inside `next`/`complete` (the artifact has no timing) and whether host permission or hook layers see those script-run model-written commands (they run inside the ShipLoop process).
How often test-spec must report revise to add an ID the step plan's focused row did not list (duty 1); n=1 case with one ID.
Whether `Unknown skill: until-loop` is specific to the harness's --plugin-dir install or happens on normal installs.
